..
Issued at 533 AM CDT Wed Sep 9 2026

Vigorous upper level trough noted on water vapor imagery over 
the northern Plains early morning with an attendant upper level 
jet extending from WY to Lake Superior. Evening ROABs sampled a 
nearly 100kt jet in this area. Convection continues to develop 
over IA early this morning, in the broad, divergent right 
entrance region of this jet. Objective analysis data depicts a 
reservoir of 1000+ J/kg of MUCAPE across IA with a 40+ kt low 
level jet aimed right into IA. As this convection develops and 
pushes eastward into northern IL cloud tops have been rapidly 
warming and convection diminishing as it moves east of the nose 
of the LLJ and encounters a substantially more stable air mass. 

A pair of small MCVs are evident on regional WSR-88d mosaic, 
one moving into NW IL just after 07z and a second one over 
central IA. The area of rain associated with that lead MCV is 
likely to continue weakening and probably gradually dry up as it
reaches lake Michigan. However, this lead MCV will likely 
increase moisture in the low-mid levels of the atmosphere and 
should allow for the second MCV to maintain itself better as it 
moves into and across northern IL later this morning. Still 
anticipate minimal instability, but a second wave of rain and 
perhaps a couple of isolated thunderstorms (especially western 
CWA) should move across northern IL and extreme northwest IN in 
the 11-15z time frame. 

While the second MCV and its associated rain shield should tend
to weaken later this morning, remnant cloud cover and footprint
of rain cooled air will likely result in the effective frontal 
boundary being pushed into our southern CWA by this afternoon. 
Cannot rule out some showers continuing into our southern CWA 
later this morning into the early afternoon, but coverage is 
expected to be on the decrease. Renewed convective development 
this afternoon appears unlikely across IL given the lack of 
forcing and weak instability. 

Another shortwave over the northern Rockies is expected to 
shear rapidly eastward into the lower Missouri River Valley 
later tonight, likely resulting in an uptick in coverage of 
showers and thunderstorms over Missouri late tonight. As this 
activity pushes east into Illinois, it is possible that the 
northern flanks of the showers could scrape across our far 
southern CWA late tonight into Thursday morning, but the vast 
majority of this rain and all of the associated thunderstorm 
activity should stay south of our area. 

Temperatures today will be heavily dictated by cloud cover with
highs potentially topping out in the lower 80s far southern CWA
prior to thicker cloud cover and potential showers. Also, far 
northwest CWA could see highs in the lower 80s assuming some 
partial clearing this afternoon. Over the majority of the CWA, 
highs will probably hold in the 70s given the cloud cover. 

Other than the small chance of showers near/south of Highway 24
in the morning, Thursday looks to be a pretty nice day weather-
wise across the area. Skies are expected to clear out, lower 
dewpoints will advect in, and highs will top out in the 70s. By 
Thursday night, the center of the high pressure ridge should set
up over the area. This should set the stage for nearly ideal 
radiational cooling with clear skies and calm winds. Have nudge 
low temps downward Thursday night, especially in the typical 
cool spots where lows could dip into the 40s. The urban heat 
island should keep the heat of the city of Chicago in the lower 
60s for low temps. Friday looks like another spectacular early 
autumn day with highs around 80, low humidity, and sunny skies. 

The weekend forecast overall looks ok, though forecast 
confidence is a bit lower with some chance it could rain a bit 
at some point. Another trough is expected to pass well north of 
the area over the weekend with a weakening cold front reaching 
the area Saturday or Saturday night before probably washing out 
altogether. Cannot totally rule out a few showers with that 
front, but given weak frontal convergence, antecedent dry air 
mass, and minimal upper forcing, the more likely scenario looks 
to be dry weather for most. Southerly winds in advance of this 
front should allow temps to warm more solidly into the 80s on 
Saturday. Another trough is expected to move into the region 
early next week bringing what looks to be a somewhat better 
chance of showers and thunderstorms in the Monday/Tuesday time 
frame. There is still model variability in the timing and track 
of that trough, so forecast confidence is still on the lower end
of the spectrum.

-Izzi
